summary: This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to bar group and individual health plans from imposing any deductibles, copays, or coinsurance on diagnostic or supplemental breast examinations, effective for plan years beginning in 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates that private health plans cover certain breast examinations without cost-sharing. It contains no provisions for federal appropriations, direct spending, or changes to government budgets. Any indirect fiscal effects (e.g., via tax-preferred HSAs) are incidental and not the focus of the legislation.

The bill adds a safe-harbor provision under IRC Section 223 so that high-deductible health plans do not lose HSA eligibility if they waive the deductible for the specified breast exams. This is a narrow technical adjustment to existing tax rules rather than a change in tax rates, deductions, or revenue policy.

The core purpose of the bill is to amend the Public Health Service Act (and related ACA and IRC provisions) to prohibit cost-sharing for diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations in private group and individual health plans. This expands mandated benefits and reduces patient out-of-pocket costs, constituting a moderate regulatory intervention in the private insurance market that aligns with the public/universal-coverage end of the spectrum.
